kyoto_muromachi_yui.gf_detail: Ask. A single omakase kaiseki course with dashi-based soups, sushi, tempura and grilled dishes; no gluten information (official site; 2025–2026 reviews).
kyoto_muromachi_yui.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a kaiseki of fish, shellfish, crab and dashi (2025–2026 reviews).
kyoto_muromachi_yui.hours_raw: 17:00–20:30 (last entry); closed Wednesday (official site; Tabelog). Reservation only, by the day before; by phone or web (official site; Tabelog). One omakase course (Tabelog shop text), ¥30,000 at a first visit (July 2025; August 2026). 10 seats at a curved counter looking onto a garden; the room can be hired for up to 20; designated smoking area (Tabelog; February 2026). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners) (Tabelog). In a townhouse on Oshikoji-dori west of Karasuma; 3 min walk from Karasuma Oike Stn exit 2 (Tabelog). Opened 15 December 2019 (Tabelog).
kyoto_muromachi_yui.notes: [Kaiseki · Karasuma Oike, 前田一光's counter by a garden] A 10-seat curved counter in a townhouse on quiet Oshikoji, facing a garden, where 前田一光 — born in Gifu to a restaurant family — serves one omakase kaiseki a night (about ¥30,000) built from that morning's market and Tango fish: playful dishes like corn-wrapped prawn tempura, then clay-pot rice with nine or ten side dishes to graze. Reviewers describe it as holding two Michelin stars. Book by the day before; last entry 20:30; closed Wednesday.

roles: Owner (店主, official site)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: 前田一光 (MAEDA KAZUTERU) was born in Nakatsugawa, Gifu, and grew up in the kitchen of the restaurant run by a parent ("料理屋を営む父親のもと"); after high school, trained in Kyoto aiming to equal that father; became owner of 室町 唯 in December 2019. The site describes visits to the market every morning, daily contact with Tango fishing ports, a counter built so guests watch the cooking, and a garden view. Reviewers in June–August 2026 say the restaurant holds two Michelin stars; a June 2026 reviewer describes a head chef and a wine-loving owner who joined guests for a drink, and says regulars sometimes bring their own wine.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: "唯一無二の食事を目指して" — food that can only be had here; nothing used that the kitchen is not satisfied with; menus not bound by convention.
chef_bio.specialty: Omakase kaiseki; clay-pot rice with many side dishes.

anecdotes.text: "What stood out the most was the variety of about 9 different accompaniments for the rice, all available for unlimited servings." — February 2026.
"I was lucky that there was a large supply of tuna caught by a customer, so we could have unlimited servings of tuna rice bowl." — June 2026.
"They wrapped the shrimp in the corn after steaming and cooling it, then tempura-fried it, which created an interesting texture." — August 2026.
"The chef is from Gifu, so we enjoyed Hoba Sushi and plenty of hairy crab." — June 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (muromachi-yui.jp): 京都烏丸御池の会席料理店、17:00〜20:30 (最終入店)、水曜定休、完全予約制、唯一無二の食事を目指して、市場に毎朝通い最高の食材だけを仕入れ、丹後の漁港と毎朝連絡、既成概念に捉われない献立、カウンター中心の内装と庭、季節に合わせた煎茶、ビンテージも含む日本酒、店主 前田一光 (MAEDA KAZUTERU): 岐阜県中津川市生まれ、料理屋を営む父親のもと幼少期から調理場に入る、高校卒業後に京都で修行、2019年12月に室町 唯の店主に就任。食べログ (店舗会員): 日本料理、中京区押小路通烏丸西入金吹町459、烏丸御池駅2番出口から徒歩3分、完全予約制 (前日まで)、おまかせコースのみ、10席 (カウンター)、貸切20名まで、カード可、2019年12月15日オープン。口コミ (2025年7月〜2026年9月、英語): コース30,000円、ミシュラン二つ星、ご飯のお供9〜10種、朴葉寿司、毛蟹、とうもろこしで巻いた海老の天ぷら、庭の見える曲線のカウンター。

cultural_comfort.note: Book by the day before; one omakase course at a counter; cards accepted.

kyoto_kentan_horibe.gf_detail: Ask. Kyoto kaiseki of dashi-based soups, mackerel sushi, sashimi with soy-based dips, grilled and fried fish, simmered beef and rice with tsukudani; no gluten information (official site; 2025–2026 reviews).
kyoto_kentan_horibe.vegan_detail: Not vegan: courses are built on fish, soft-shelled turtle, Omi beef and dashi (2025–2026 reviews).
kyoto_kentan_horibe.hours_raw: Lunch 11:30–12:30 last entry, closes 14:00; dinner 18:00–19:30 last entry, closes 22:00; closed Tuesday; reservation required (official site; Tabelog gives slightly different last entries). Phone bookings 14:00–17:00, or TableCheck; changes or cancellations by phone at least three days ahead; cancellation fees 25% two days before, 50% the day before, 100% on the day (official site). Even when Tabelog shows full, seats may be free by phone or the website (Tabelog). Dress code: no sweatpants, jeans, shorts or sandals; cover tattoos; no strong perfume (Tabelog). Children below elementary school age only in private rooms (Tabelog). 14 seats at a counter and tables, plus private rooms for 4–6 with a room charge of 10–20% of the food (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners), no e-money or QR (Tabelog). In a townhouse on Nishikikoji west of Muromachi; 4 min walk from Shijo Stn / Karasuma Stn exits 22 and 24 (official site). Opened here 10 December 2016 (Tabelog).
kyoto_kentan_horibe.notes: [Kaiseki · Shijo Karasuma, 堀部努's Kyoto cuisine] A townhouse kaiseki restaurant on Nishikikoji with a small garden, a counter and private rooms, where 堀部努 — who cooked in Gion, at Gion Horibe, before moving here — serves monthly Kyoto courses: soft-shelled turtle soup, sea bream from Akashi, fried hamo with figs, a hassun in a basket. Lunch ¥12,000, dinner ¥25,000, tax and service included; Tabelog also sells pricier "courses for foreign guests". Michelin one star nine years running, per its site. Dress smartly; closed Tuesday.

roles: Owner-chef (店主, official site)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: 研覃 (けんたん) means to pursue and explore deeply and to cultivate oneself; the owner signs as 店主 堀部 努; site news marks a Michelin one star for nine years running (July 2026) and the restaurant’s twentieth anniversary (August 2026). A September 2026 reviewer names the chef as Tsutomu Horibe, who honed skills in Gion and at "Gion Horibe" before moving to Karasuma; Tabelog dates this site from 10 December 2016. A November 2025 regular notes foreign guests at lunch; a July 2026 reviewer says the owner-chef and staff always seem to enjoy their work.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: to serve the world through cooking for the guest’s "delicious!", and to grow as people.
chef_bio.specialty: Seasonal Kyoto kaiseki; hassun; soft-shelled turtle soup.

anecdotes.text: "Upon entering, the owner personally greeted us, and there was a natural warmth in the way the dishes were presented." — November 2025.
"I asked about it, and they told me they grind the conger twice—a truly labor-intensive dish." — of the hamo surinagashi, August 2026.
"The owner-chef and the staff always seemed to be enjoying their work, which left a lasting impression." — July 2026.
A November 2025 group of five paid ¥12,000 each for lunch plus a 5% private-room fee and found the hospitality worth it.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (kyoto-horibe.com): 研覃 (けんたん) とは「深ク深ク追求スル、探求スル。又自分自身ヲ耕シ研鑽スル」という意、店主 堀部 努、昼餉12,000円・夕餉25,000円 (税・サ込)、昼11時30分〜12時30分 (最終入店) 14時閉店、夜18時00分〜19時30分 (最終入店) 22時閉店、火曜定休、電話予約は14時〜17時、TableCheck、キャンセル料 (2日前25%、前日50%、当日100%)、一つ星9年連続 (2026年7月)、二十周年 (2026年8月)、おせち、四条駅・烏丸駅22番・24番出口から徒歩4分。食べログ (店舗会員): 日本料理・海鮮・創作、中京区錦小路通室町西入ル天神山町273、外国人のお客様限定コース 昼15,000円 (現金のみ)・夜28,000円、ドレスコード、タトゥーは隠す、未就学児は個室のみ、14席、個室あり (個室料10〜20%)、カード可、2016年12月10日オープン、店舗紹介: 京都の五味・五色・五法、町家と坪庭。口コミ (2025年11月〜2026年9月、英語): 祇園時代からの名店、すっぽんと玉子豆腐の椀、Akashi の鯛、鱧の揚げ物と Joyo のいちじく、Omi beef、Tango のお米、八寸、杉板焼き。

cultural_comfort.note: Book ahead (phone 14:00–17:00 or TableCheck); smart dress; Tabelog sells separate, pricier courses for foreign guests.

kyoto_itameshi_oliva.gf_detail: Ask. Pasta, risotto, gratin with bread and fried olives stuffed with meat dominate; carpaccio, prosciutto and roasts are also served; no gluten information (2024–2026 reviews).
kyoto_itameshi_oliva.vegan_detail: Ask. Most dishes use seafood, meat or cheese; seasonal vegetable and fruit appetizers appear, but no vegan dish is named (Tabelog; 2024–2026 reviews).
kyoto_itameshi_oliva.hours_raw: Monday, Tuesday and Friday–Sunday 17:00–24:00; Thursday 19:00–24:00; closed Wednesday (Tabelog). Reservations by phone (Tabelog) or Instagram DM (June 2026); a ¥1,000 per-person fee for same-day no-shows; at least one food item and one drink each; a 120-minute limit when busy (Tabelog). 12 seats: a 5-seat counter and small tables (Tabelog). Prices shown before tax; no charge (Tabelog). Cards and e-money (Tabelog). English menu (Tabelog). Third floor of the 先斗町たばこやビル: from Pontocho, take alley no. 15 on the north side and the lift to 3F (Tabelog). 3 min from Kawaramachi Stn (Tabelog). Opened 2 August 2017 (Tabelog).
kyoto_itameshi_oliva.notes: [Italian · Pontocho, a third-floor hideaway with Wakasa produce] A twelve-seat Italian up a lift in the Tabakoya building, reached from Pontocho's alley no. 15. The owner-chef is from Obama in Fukui and builds the menu around Wakasa fish, seasonal produce and Wakasa rice: start with the antipasto platter or prosciutto and mozzarella, then the squid-ink risotto, a seasonal pasta, oyster gratin or the lamb steak, and panna cotta. Portions are generous and good for sharing; the owner will cook off-menu on request. About ¥14,000 for two with wine (July 2025). Book by phone; closed Wednesday, open to midnight.

roles: Owner-chef (unnamed; November 2024 reviews: "The owner is from Obama in Fukui", "The owner-chef is friendly")
chef_bio.origin: Obama, Fukui Prefecture (November 2024 and February 2025 reviews).
chef_bio.background: Tabelog's introduction describes fresh seafood and seasonal ingredients from Wakasa in Obama City, Fukui Prefecture, and risotto of Wakasa rice. Tabelog gives the opening as 2 August 2017.
chef_bio.specialty: Squid-ink risotto; seasonal pasta; fried stuffed olives.

anecdotes.text: A July 2025 diner found the owner running the room alone because the staff member was off sick, with four groups in.
A November 2024 regular named the squid-ink risotto "a flavor bomb" and the meat-stuffed fried olives a perfect match for Italian beer.
A May 2025 reviewer notes the place is popular with foreign tourists, so phone booking is essential, and that the owner will make dishes not on the menu.

kyoto_men_kui_kin_ya.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: handmade wheat udon and battered tempura and kushikatsu (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).
kyoto_men_kui_kin_ya.vegan_detail: Ask. A February 2025 reviewer says the shop offers vegan options and English menus, but the standard broth is bonito and kombu dashi (2025–2026 reviews).
kyoto_men_kui_kin_ya.hours_raw: Tabelog: Monday–Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday 11:30–15:40 and 18:00–19:40; closed Thursday and Friday. An October 2025 review instead gives 11:30–20:00 (last order 19:30), closed Monday (or the next day after a holiday). No reservations; queues at times (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews). 15 seats (7 counter, two tables for 4); non-smoking (Tabelog). No cards; e-money and QR payments accepted (Tabelog). On a corner of the Miyagawacho tea-house streets, marked by a large lantern; 5 min from Gion-Shijo Stn (Tabelog; April 2026).
kyoto_men_kui_kin_ya.notes: [Udon · Miyagawacho, handmade flat udon by the tea houses] A small handmade-udon counter on a corner of Miyagawacho's tea-house streets, under a big lantern, five minutes from Gion-Shijo Stn. The owner makes the noodles: thin, flat and glossy, from Kyoto wheat, boiled to order and served in a clear bonito-and-kombu broth. Kake udon from ¥650; the Kujo negi tempura with cold udon (¥1,300) and the tempura bowls are the popular orders. Reviews split on the tempura — some find it light and crisp, an August 2026 diner found it greasy — but agree on the noodles. Many guests are visitors from abroad; English menu. Hours vary between sources; check before going.

roles: Owner, who researches and makes the noodles by hand (Tabelog)
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog's introduction: the owner researches and makes the noodles by hand; tempura and kushikatsu are specialities; the shop sits in Miyagawacho among tea houses. An April 2025 reviewer saw the udon being made, to the delight of tourists.
chef_bio.specialty: Handmade flat udon; Kujo negi tempura.

anecdotes.text: A February 2025 reviewer noted that 70–80% of the customers were from abroad and that the shop offers English menus and vegan options.
An August 2026 diner praised the flat Kyoto-wheat udon but found the tempura greasy and the chicken tough: "Just come for the udon."
An August 2026 visitor liked the burdock and onion tempura (¥180 each) so much with a little salt that it never went into the udon.

kyoto_cafe_de_corazon.gf_detail: Ask. House-made tarts, cheesecake, cookies, parfaits, French toast and toast; no gluten information (2026 reviews).
kyoto_cafe_de_corazon.vegan_detail: Ask. Black coffee suits, but the sweets use cream, cheese and eggs (2026 reviews).
kyoto_cafe_de_corazon.hours_raw: 10:00–17:00, Monday–Saturday; closed Sunday and the third Monday (Tabelog). No seat reservations, but cakes can be held (Tabelog). Cash only (Tabelog: payment changed to cash only; September 2026). 8 counter seats; non-smoking; one parking space (Tabelog; October 2026). Takeaway: coffee beans, baked goods, coffee jelly (Tabelog; September 2026). 8–9 min walk from Imadegawa Stn (2026 reviews). Opened 12 June 2012 (Tabelog).
kyoto_cafe_de_corazon.notes: [Café · Nishijin, an eight-seat roastery counter] A counter café in a residential lane of Nishijin, opened in 2012 by Katsushi Kawaguchi, who trained and served as manager at the famed Cafe Bach in Tokyo's Minami-Senju, with the owner's wife, a pastry chef. About 20 house-roasted, hand-sorted beans are brewed to order; cakes, tarts and seasonal parfaits come from the wife's oven; seasonal paintings change on the walls. Coffee from about ¥930 (October 2026), cheesecake ¥450. Eight seats, no seat bookings, cash only. Closed Sunday and the third Monday.

chef_bio.chef_name: Katsushi Kawaguchi (romaji from a September 2026 review; the kanji is not in a source)

A September 2026 visitor bought the coffee jelly to take away; it separated before reaching the hotel but still tasted delicious.
An October 2026 diner found coffee from ¥930 a bit pricey but enjoyed it from a Wedgwood mug and a long chat with the owner.

kyoto_songbird_coffee.gf_detail: Ask. The signature curry comes with rice, fried onions and a soft-boiled egg, while the egg sandwiches use buttered bread; no gluten information (2026 reviews).
kyoto_songbird_coffee.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the signature dishes are built on egg (the thick omelette sandwich, the curry's soft-boiled egg), with butter, cheese and chicken (2026 reviews).
kyoto_songbird_coffee.hours_raw: 10:00–18:30, last order 18:00; closed Thursday; hours may change (Tabelog). No reservations; a wait at lunch (October 2026). 25 seats: a counter of single boxes, tables for 2, 4 and 6; non-smoking; children and prams welcome (Tabelog; October, November 2026). Cards, IC cards and QR payments (Tabelog). Egg sandwiches to take away (October 2026). Second floor of SONGBIRD DESIGN STORE, near Nijo Castle; 7–8 min from Nijojo-mae Stn (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). kyoto_songbird_coffee.notes: [Café · Nijo Castle, curry and egg sandwiches above a design store] A café on the second floor of SONGBIRD DESIGN STORE near Nijo Castle, furnished with the studio's own furniture and goods (some for sale). The two dishes everyone orders are the SONGBIRD curry — a cylinder of rice crowned with a soft-boiled egg and crisp onions — and the hot, thick egg sandwich on buttered bread; the half-and-half lunch (¥1,650) gets both. Coffee comes from roasters around Japan; the hojicha banana shake is a big glass. Expect a short queue at lunch. Open 10:00–18:30, closed Thursday.

kyoto_kameya_kiyonaga.gf_detail: Ask. The signature seijō kankidan is a rice- and wheat-flour dough fried in sesame oil (an October 2026 review), and the shop lists wheat flour among its main ingredients (official notice); other sweets are bean paste and chestnut, with no ingredient list published.
kyoto_kameya_kiyonaga.vegan_detail: Ask. Bean-paste and fried sweets such as the seijō kankidan may suit, but no ingredient list is published, and the dorayaki and kintsuba are not described (official site; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_kameya_kiyonaga.hours_raw: 8:30–17:00; closed Wednesday and some other days — in November 2026 also the 12th and 19th (Thursdays) (official site). Tabelog gives 8:30–17:30. Takeaway shop; orders by phone or the online shop for delivery (official site). Cards, e-money and QR (Tabelog). On the south side of the stone steps below Yasaka Shrine — face the west gate and turn right without crossing Higashioji-dori (official site); 460 m from Gion-Shijo Stn (Tabelog).
kyoto_kameya_kiyonaga.notes: [Wagashi · Gion, a confectioner since 1617] A Kyoto sweets house founded in 1617, now facing Yasaka Shrine's west gate, that has supplied temples and shrines for centuries. Its signature, the seijō kankidan, is a Nara-period Tang sweet — a hard, pouch-shaped dough of rice and wheat flour around spiced bean paste, fried in sesame oil (¥750 each). Also kintsuba, chestnut sweets and seasonal fresh sweets. Closed Wednesday and some Thursdays.

roles: Operator: 亀屋清永 (company); no person named
chef_bio.background: Per the official history page: founded, by tradition, in 1617 (Genna 3), living at Teramachi-Sanjo with the trade name 亀屋冶兵衛 before taking the name 亀屋清永; listed in 1842 among the confectioners supplying the Imperial Palace; the seijō kankidan descends from the Tang confections brought by envoys in the Nara period and is called the root of Kyoto sweets. Tabelog Japanese-sweets WEST "Tabelog 100" 2026. In October–November 2026 the shop sold its seijō kankidan and buto at the 78th Shōsōin exhibition in Nara (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Seijō kankidan; buto.

anecdotes.text: Plaques inside show supply to Chion-in, Yasaka Shrine, Enryaku-ji and Nanzen-ji — October 2026.

kyoto_tsuneya_densuke.gf_detail: Ask. Over a hundred à la carte dishes — sashimi, grilled fish, saba sushi, tempura, fried conger and whale, miso dengaku, bear hot pot; no gluten information (official site; 2026 reviews).

kyoto_tsuneya_densuke.notes: [Kappo izakaya · south of the Imperial Palace, a hundred dishes and bear hot pot] A small izakaya on a quiet corner near the palace, open about 25 years, with no set courses: pick from over a hundred seasonal dishes — a famous sashimi platter, shirokuji, thick saba sushi, hamo shabu, and its rare bear hot pot. kyoto_sushi_obino.gf_detail: Ask. Edomae sushi with soy-brushed nigiri, small dishes with miso and egg-yolk vinegar, and a soup; no gluten information is published (official site; 2022–26 reviews).

kyoto_sushi_obino.hours_raw: 17:00–21:00, last entry 19:30; closed irregularly (official site; Tabelog lists every day 17:00–21:00). Bookings via the web or by email; the courses no longer start all at once — come at any time (official site). Lunch teyui-zushi is described on the official site; no lunch hours are given. 8 counter seats; non-smoking; cards; children welcome, with a children’s menu; tell the shop ahead about a stroller (Tabelog; official site). At the back of the 若葉ビル on the east side of Tomikoji north of Nishiki (south of Takoyakushi); 7 min from Shijo Stn, 5 min from Hankyu Kawaramachi Stn (official site). kyoto_sushi_obino.notes: [Sushi · Tomikoji-Nishiki, counter sushi made approachable] An eight-seat Edomae counter at the back of a building on Tomikoji just north of Nishiki, opened in 2020 and reworked in 2023 to make counter sushi easier for younger and overseas guests: a ¥6,000 course by its young artisans, the head chef's course from ¥12,000, and no fixed start time. The owner is a sommelier and pairs sake — served at chosen temperatures — or, unusually, red wine with the sushi. The official site also describes a teyui-zushi lunch of hand-rolls you assemble, toasting the nori over charcoal (¥4,800). Booking advised.

roles: Owner-sommelier (2022 reviews; official site: ソムリエ) and a head chef (大将), with young artisans for the ¥6,000 course (official site); no names on the site
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: opened in October 2020 during the pandemic; from September 2023 the single omakase with a simultaneous start was replaced by more affordable courses at any time, including a ¥6,000 course made by a different artisan from the head chef, to pass on counter-sushi culture to younger and overseas guests; young or less experienced staff are hired as sushi artisans; fish is bought through a partner wholesaler. An October 2022 review names the chef then as Mr. Kosakai, of the Sushi Masuda line; a March 2023 review links the shop to the Sukiyabashi Jiro and Sushi Masuda lineage.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: "もっとカウンター鮨を多くの方に知っていただきたい" — to make counter sushi known to more people, with some tension but no stiffness.
chef_bio.specialty: Edomae nigiri with sake or red-wine pairing; teyui-zushi lunch.

anecdotes.text: A January 2026 visitor who added the wine pairing found the chef explaining the origins of each sake and sushi in detail.

kyoto_clay_pot_curry_ohmiya.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the curry sauce starts from a bouillon made over a day, and every curry on the menu carries meat or seafood (official site).
kyoto_clay_pot_curry_ohmiya.hours_raw: Lunch 11:30–15:00 (to 15:30 at weekends and holidays) and dinner 17:30–21:00 (last order 20:30); closed irregularly; may close early when ingredients run out (official site; Tabelog). Order by QR code: curry, spice level, rice size and toppings (September 2026). 16–17 seats: counter and small tables (Tabelog; official site); non-smoking; cards, e-money and QR; takeaway and delivery; menu in English, Chinese and Korean; children welcome, with a children’s curry (Tabelog; official site). On the 2nd floor of the 辨天堂ビル on the Shinkyogoku arcade south of Rokkaku, with a lift; 5 min from exit 9 of Kyoto Kawaramachi Stn (official site; Tabelog). Opened here 11 August 2023 after 14 years at Marutamachi (official site; Tabelog).
kyoto_clay_pot_curry_ohmiya.notes: [Curry · Shinkyogoku, European curry bubbling in clay pots] A second-floor curry shop on the Shinkyogoku arcade that moved here in 2023 after 14 years at Marutamachi (once known as 近江屋清右衛門), sister to SOUP CURRY OHMIYA. The curry — a day-long bouillon, house-roasted curry powder and two days of simmering with fruit and red wine — arrives still bubbling in a clay pot. The beef rib in demi-glace (¥1,650) is the one everyone orders; Kyoto-beef, Tanba Kogen pork cutlet and keema are the local-ingredient options. Order by QR code; a September 2026 visitor saw one chef and one staff member at work, so book at weekends.

roles: Owner (unnamed; the official site says the owner chose the Kyoto beef personally); one chef and one staff member on a September 2026 visit
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: a European-style curry specialist that ran for 14 years at Marutamachi before moving to Shinkyogoku; former name 欧風土鍋カレー近江屋清右衛門 (Tabelog); the sister shop is SOUP CURRY OHMIYA (in data as kyoto_soup_curry_ohmiya); for the beef curry the owner ate around Kyoto’s beef and chose certified 京の肉 from Kyoto Tanba-Kameoka. The invoice number on Tabelog is T3130001077204.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: a handmade curry that takes a day for the bouillon and two days for the sauce.
chef_bio.specialty: Beef rib demi-glace curry; Kyoto-beef curry.

kyoto_dessert_cafe_chourakukan.notes: [Café · Maruyama Park, tea in a Meiji mansion] The café of the Chourakukan, a stone Western-style mansion of 1909 beside Maruyama Park, built as a guest house by a tobacco magnate. Add 10% service. Open daily 11:00–18:30.

kyoto_kawamichiya_ginka.hours_raw: Official site and Tabelog: 11:30–24:00 (last order 23:30), closed Wednesday; the official Pontocho page also says the shop opens from 17:00 to suit the evening street, and an October 2026 diner noted it now closes around midnight rather than later. A little west of Pontocho Park, midway along Pontocho (official site).
kyoto_kawamichiya_ginka.notes: [Soba · Pontocho, since 1902, open till midnight] An old-fashioned soba shop just off Pontocho Park, one of three houses that branched from 総本家河道屋 in 1902: herring soba, duck nanban with Kujo leek, tempura soba and grated-daikon soba in a rich bonito broth, with green onions served on the side. Kake soba ¥880, tempura soba ¥2,000 (2026). Run by father and son, per a September 2026 diner. 11:30–24:00, closed Wednesday; no bookings; smoking allowed.

roles: Family owners (unnamed): the current head and a son, per a September 2026 review
chef_bio.background: Per the official site (2017 page): Kawamichiya Ginka branched from 総本家河道屋 in 1902 (Meiji 35); the head house had three daughters, who married craftsmen trained at Kawamichiya and were given the house names 金華, 銀華 and 銅華 to branch out. Ginka first ran a soba shop at Kiyamachi-Sanjo; in the second generation it closed during the Pacific War, and the third generation reopened it at the present site on Pontocho. A September 2026 diner understood the current owner to be the fourth generation, with a son working alongside, and noted green onions served on a separate plate, appreciated by overseas guests; a February 2026 diner described a quite elderly owner.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: aiming for a taste found only in this shop, unchanged since the founding.
chef_bio.specialty: Nishin soba; duck nanban; tempura soba.

anecdotes.text: A September 2026 diner on a ninth dinner of the day overheard the son chatting with the father over a staff meal, and found the bonito dashi "incredibly rich".

kyoto_issen_yoshoku_honten.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the batter is made with dashi and topped with bonito flakes, eggs, chikuwa and domestic wagyu (official site). Tabelog’s "vegetarian options" tag is not borne out by the official recipe.
kyoto_issen_yoshoku_honten.hours_raw: Official site: Gion honten open every day — weekdays 11:00–1:00, Saturdays and days before holidays 11:00–3:00, Sundays and holidays 10:30–22:00; Tabelog gives Friday and Saturday to 3:00. No reservations (Tabelog). One main dish only, the Issen Yoshoku, ¥950 with a choice of sweet, normal (sweet-and-spicy) or spicy sauce (official menu). 100 seats; non-smoking; children welcome (Tabelog). Cards and PayPay (Tabelog). Takeaway, a counter in Takashimaya Kyoto B1F, and mail order (official site). At the corner of Shijo and Nawate, beside the police box; 1 min from Keihan Gion-Shijo Stn exit 7 (official site; Tabelog).
kyoto_issen_yoshoku_honten.notes: [Issen yoshoku · Shijo-Nawate, Gion's late-night snack] The 100-seat Gion shop that revived issen yoshoku, the pre-war flour snack seen as okonomiyaki's ancestor: a thin dashi batter folded over Kujo leek, egg, konnyaku, chikuwa and wagyu, sauced sweet, normal or spicy — the only dish, ¥950. Inside, tongue-in-cheek risqué ema, figures and kimono-clad mannequins at the tables play on the old pleasure quarter. Open daily from 11:00 to 1:00 (3:00 on Saturdays and days before holidays); a counter in Takashimaya and mail order too.

roles: 株式会社壹錢洋食 (founding president 木下辰雄, per the official site)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: issen yoshoku faded in the late Showa era as modern okonomiyaki took over; the company’s first president, 木下辰雄, set out to revive it and make it better, choosing Kujo leek, egg and domestic wagyu, working on the seasoned konnyaku, dashi and sauce, and using shredded nori so that it would not cling to the teeth. It was first sold in a small shop by the Shirakawa in Gion, popular with maiko, geiko and entertainers, then moved to the larger shop at Shijo-Nawate, where the playful decor — saucy ema and figures satirising love in the pleasure quarter — became a sight in itself; mail order on Rakuten from April 2011. The site lists two shops today, the Gion honten and Takashimaya Kyoto, and sales at Mitsui Outlet Park Shiga Ryuo. Okonomiyaki "Tabelog 100" 2018.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: "that nostalgic taste once more — and even better."
chef_bio.specialty: Issen Yoshoku (one dish only).

anecdotes.text: "Interestingly, I was seated at the same table as a mannequin." — October 2026; the price is now ¥950.
An August 2026 diner remembered it at ¥600–700 and found ¥950 steep for a dish that was once a cheap snack.
"We will prepare the Issen for you," without any hesitation — there is only one dish (October 2026).

kyoto_chidori_tei.notes: [Sushi · Gion, Kyoto saba sushi and box sushi] A small, old-fashioned sushi house on Donguri-dori near Gion-Shijo Stn, serving the Kyoto styles: thick, soft saba sushi, conger-eel box sushi, kombu-wrapped rolls and, in winter, piping-hot steamed sushi. The "Wakasa" set (¥2,730) samples most of them with a clear soup; in summer there are hamo and ayu sushi. Saba sushi travels well as a takeaway. The owner is friendly and the chawanmushi has fans of its own. Lunch to 17:00 only; cash only; closed Thursday.

kyoto_le_petit_mec_imadegawa.notes: [Bakery · Imadegawa, the red-fronted French bakery] Le Petit Mec's first shop, opened in 1998 on Imadegawa-dori in Nishijin and nicknamed "Aka Mec" for its red door and awning. Inside it smells of butter and plays French radio-style music; pick your breads, pay, and eat them at the tables, where they are warmed and sliced for you. The croissants are the stars (au beurre ¥270, almond ¥430, Earl Grey), with hard breads, fruit pies and seasonal specials. Busy from the morning; open daily 8:00–18:00.

kyoto_yumeya_kawabata_nijo.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: okonomiyaki batter, negiyaki and yakisoba are wheat-based, with sweet sauces (2026 reviews).
kyoto_yumeya_kawabata_nijo.vegan_detail: Not vegan: okonomiyaki with pork, beef, squid and egg, topped with fish flakes (2026 reviews).
kyoto_yumeya_kawabata_nijo.hours_raw: 17:00–21:00, last order 20:30; closed Wednesday; closes when sold out (Tabelog). Reservations taken and advised (Tabelog; May 2026). 45 seats, with sofa and tatami seats; the whole room can be hired for 20–50 people; non-smoking (Tabelog). Cash only — no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog). Paid parking next door (Tabelog). On Kawabata-dori at Nijo, by the Kamo River, under red lanterns; 3 min from Kyoto Shiyakusho-mae Stn, 5 min from Sanjo Stn (Tabelog; June 2026).
kyoto_yumeya_kawabata_nijo.notes: [Okonomiyaki · Kawabata Nijo, fluffy yam okonomiyaki by the Kamo River] A long-running okonomiyaki and teppan house under red lanterns on Kawabata-dori, its walls signed by many celebrities. The house style is soft and fluffy, thanks to plenty of yam in the batter: the Yume-yaki (¥1,480), layered rather than mixed, and the Fukafuka, piled with beef, pork and squid, both finished with white flakes from Ehime. Add a thin-noodle salt yakisoba and teppan sides such as tonpei or gizzard. Dishes arrive cooked. Cash only; 17:00–21:00, closed Wednesday; it closes when sold out, so book.
